title: The Young Wolf
timeline: Month 6, 298 AC. Winterfell to the Twins.
summary: Bran wakes with no legs and no memory. A raven comes from the south saying the Hand of the King is a traitor, and the boy who is now Lord of Winterfell calls his father's banners. Winterfell fills with two thousand men in three days. Torren rides south in the middle of the largest thing that has ever happened to him, learns what it costs to cross a river, and is standing in the yard at the Twins when the army is cut in half on purpose.

scenes.title: The Boy on the Bed
scenes.stage_directions: CANON: Bran wakes after weeks, crippled, with no memory of the fall; the catspaw assassin's attempt has already happened and Summer has already killed him. Torren has been on the door since the catspaw got past the guard, which is his failure and is treated as one. Small, quiet, three-room scene. Winterfell is half empty and cold and Act 1's crowd is conspicuously gone. Composer: the Act 1 Winterfell theme, same melody, one instrument, minor.

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: A man came up this stair with a knife while you were on the door, and got past you, and it was a wolf that stopped him and not you. Nobody has said a word about it. You have been on this door for nineteen days.

n2.speaker: hune
n2.text: Nineteen days, ser. You'll take a relief today whether you want one.

n3.speaker: hune
n3.text: I know you do. That's not a reason, that's a penance, and penance is no good to a lad on a door. Four hours. Then come back.

n4.speaker: hune
n4.text: You should. So should I, and so should the four men on the outer stair, and so should whoever left a window open in a castle full of strangers. That's six of us and one boy. Divide it up however you like, it doesn't come off him.

n5.speaker: narrator
n5.text: Inside the room, something moves that has not moved in a month.

n7.speaker: narrator
n7.text: You are the nearest man. You are always the nearest man to this boy, it turns out, and it has never once helped.

n8.speaker: bran_stark
n8.text: Ser. Ser, why can't I - what happened? Did I fall? I don't fall.

choices.text: "You fell, my lord. From the tower."
"Your lady mother's coming. She'll tell you."
"You're awake. That's the whole of what matters this morning."

n9.speaker: bran_stark
n9.direction: He says it three times over the following weeks. He is right.

n10.speaker: narrator
n10.text: She is not coming. She has been on the kingsroad for weeks and nobody has told him and you have just decided not to be the one who does.

n13.speaker: narrator
n13.text: You wait on the stair and you hear his brother start crying through two inches of oak, and then stop, very deliberately, because there is nobody left in this castle who is allowed to.

scenes.title: Two Thousand Men in Three Days
scenes.stage_directions: CANON: word of Ned's arrest reaches Winterfell; Robb calls his father's banners; the Northern lords come in. The yard's population visibly triples across three in-game days - the same level as Act 1, re-dressed with tents, forges, horse lines, mud. Six optional lord conversations, each worth a relationship that pays off in Act 5 battle dialogue. DRAMATIC IRONY: everyone here is desperate for news of Lord Stark. The player watched him be arrested one act ago and knows exactly how bad it is.
objectives: Meet the lords of the North

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: A raven from the south. The Hand of the King has confessed to treason. Lord Eddard Stark is in a cell under the Red Keep and his daughters are in the queen's hands.
n1.direction: The player already knows all of this and knows it is a lie, having been in the throne room for it. Nobody in this scene does.

n2.speaker: robb_stark
n2.text: Call the banners. All of them. Every man who owes Winterfell service - and ser, you'll write to Blackpool yourself, since you know the road.

n3.speaker: torren
n3.text: My lord, Blackpool can raise perhaps eighty men.

n4.speaker: robb_stark
n4.text: Then write for eighty. I'll take every one of them and I'll know all their names by the Neck.

n10.speaker: greatjon_umber
n10.text: BLACKPOOL! Gods, is Ondrew Slate still alive? He owes me a horse from before you were whelped.

choices.text: "He is, my lord, and he says you lost that horse at dice."

n11.speaker: greatjon_umber
n11.text: HE SAYS - ha! HA! He does, does he! Boy, you'll ride near me and you'll say things like that where I can hear them.

n12.speaker: greatjon_umber
n12.text: Well. Good. Tell him I've not forgotten.

n20.speaker: rickard_karstark
n20.text: Three sons I've brought. Harrion, Eddard, Torrhen. I'd have brought thirty if I had them.

n22.speaker: rickard_karstark
n22.text: For the King Who Knelt. There's a deal of Torrhens in the North and every one of them named for a man who gave up. Don't let it stick to you, ser.
n22.direction: The name joke, said once, plainly, by a man who will be executed for refusing to give anything up. Never referred to again in Chapter 1.

n30.speaker: maege_mormont
n30.text: You've a good hand on that horse and a terrible one on that sword. Where were you knighted?

choices.text: "A field. In the rain, my lady."

n31.speaker: maege_mormont
n31.text: Good. The ones knighted in halls are the ones I have to dig out of ditches. Grip it lower. You're strangling it.

n32.speaker: maege_mormont
n32.text: No. It matters how. Grip it lower, ser, you're strangling it.

n40.speaker: wyman_manderly
n40.text: Fifteen hundred men and a hundred lances from White Harbour, and every one of them fed better than yours. Have you eaten today, ser? You have not. I can always tell.

n50.speaker: galbart_glover
n50.text: You'll want to stop counting the tents. Everyone does it for the first day. Two thousand at Winterfell, another six on the road, twelve by Moat Cailin if the Ryswells come. It's a number and then it's men and then it's a great deal less than the number.

n60.speaker: hune
n60.text: Eighty men from Blackpool came in this morning. Your father's not with them.

n62.speaker: hune
n62.text: He sent his men and he sent his son, ser. In the North that's the whole of what a lord is for. Don't make it a slight because you'd like one.

scenes.title: Two Fingers
scenes.stage_directions: CANON: the Greatjon objects to the order of march, draws steel on Robb in his own hall, and Grey Wind takes two of his fingers; the Greatjon laughs it off and calls Robb his lord. Torren is on the lower bench, close enough to be splashed. This is the moment the player watches a boy become a commander. Composer: cut everything on the draw. Nothing under the wolf.

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: The same hall as the feast, and it has not been cleaned so much as re-used. Maps on the table where the roast was.

n2.speaker: greatjon_umber
n2.text: I'll not be put behind the Hornwoods and the Cerwyns like a baggage cart. I've eight hundred men. I'll have the van or I'll take them home.

n3.speaker: robb_stark
n3.text: You'll have the place I give you, my lord, or you'll go home and explain to your sons why the Umbers weren't there.

n4.speaker: narrator
n4.text: The Greatjon puts his hand on his knife, and the hall makes the specific sound a hundred men make when they all stop chewing at once.

n5.speaker: narrator
n5.text: Nobody sees the wolf move. That is the honest truth of it. There is a lord with a knife and then there is a lord with two fingers on the table and a great grey animal under him with a red mouth.

n6.speaker: narrator
n6.text: It goes on your sleeve. You will get it out with sand and it will not come out.

n8.speaker: greatjon_umber
n8.text: HA! Meat's tough on my hand, is it? Your father kept a wolf and I thought it a nonsense. My lord. My LORD. Bind this up before I bleed on your maps.

n9.speaker: narrator
n9.text: Everyone in the hall calls him my lord within the count of a hundred, and none of them noticed deciding to.

choices.text: Watch Robb's hands. They are steady.

n10.speaker: narrator
n10.text: His hands are steady on the table. Under the table, out of everyone's sight but yours from the lower bench, one of them is gripping the wood hard enough to whiten.

n11.speaker: narrator
n11.text: The wolf has gone back under the table and is lying with its chin on its paws like a dog by a hearth, and its eyes have not left the Greatjon once.

scenes.title: The Kingsroad South
scenes.stage_directions: CANON: the Northern host marches south to Moat Cailin and on toward the Twins. Structured as three camp interstitials with a combat tutorial in the middle - Lannister outriders scouting the column, which is Torren's first fight and is deliberately unglamorous, muddy, and over in ninety seconds. He does not kill anyone here; that is reserved for the Whispering Wood. Composer: a marching ostinato that gets a little more tired every interstitial.

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: The column is four miles long and moves at the speed of the slowest cart in it. You had imagined this differently.

n2.speaker: hune
n2.text: Here's war, ser. Walking. Then more walking. Then a bad hour. Then walking.

n10.speaker: narrator
n10.text: Moat Cailin, or what is left of it: three towers standing out of a bog that has eaten twenty. Every man in the column goes quiet passing under it and nobody can say why.

n15.speaker: hune
n15.text: Riders on the flank. Lions. Ser - shield up, feet apart, and stop thinking about how you look.

n20.speaker: narrator
n20.text: It is nothing like the yard. Nothing at all. There is mud in it and everyone is shouting and it is over before you have found your breath.

n22.speaker: narrator
n22.text: They break and ride. Nobody chases them, which surprises you until you understand: they were sent to be seen. Somebody now knows exactly where twelve thousand Northmen are.

n23.speaker: torren
n23.text: I didn't - serjeant, I don't think I hit anyone.

n24.speaker: hune
n24.text: No. Nobody does, the first time. You stood in the line and you didn't run and the man beside you didn't have to think about you. That is the entire job, ser. The killing's later and it's worse.

n25.speaker: narrator
n25.text: Nobody was counting. You count it yourself for four nights running.

n30.speaker: wells
n30.text: Blackpool. You're a long way from a wet field.

n31.speaker: torren
n31.text: Ser Emmon. You rode north with the king. Why are you riding south with a Stark?

n32.speaker: wells
n32.text: Because the king is dead and I liked him, and because the men who did for the Hand's guard in the street did it eight to one, and I have discovered that I mind that more than I expected to. It is not a better reason than yours. It is only mine.

scenes.title: The Price of a Bridge
scenes.stage_directions: CANON: Robb must cross the Green Fork; Walder Frey holds the only bridge; Catelyn goes in alone to negotiate; the price is Frey hostages, a Frey squire, Arya betrothed to a Frey son, and Robb married to a Frey daughter of Walder's choosing. Torren is on the door with Catelyn's guard and hears the terms through it. He is one of about six people who hears the marriage clause said out loud. Composer: a small, mean, pretty melody. Something that sounds like a bargain.

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: Two castles and a bridge between them, and an old man in one of them who has been waiting his entire life to be needed.

n2.speaker: galbart_glover
n2.text: Four hours she's been in there. Whatever he's asking, he's asked for it twice, and got it once.

n3.speaker: narrator
n3.text: The door is thick. You are standing at it because someone must, and you hear the shape of a very old voice enjoying itself.

choices.text: Stand your post and hear nothing.

n4.speaker: walder_frey
n4.text: ...and your son. Your son marries one of mine. A daughter, a granddaughter, I'll pick her myself when the time comes, heh, and he'll take what he's given and be glad.

n5.speaker: catelyn_stark
n5.text: He is a boy of fifteen with an army behind him. You are asking him to sell the only thing he has left to sell.

n6.speaker: walder_frey
n6.text: I'm asking him to cross my bridge. He can swim, my lady, it's free.

n7.speaker: narrator
n7.text: Robb agrees to it in about four heartbeats, because there is no other bridge in three hundred miles and because he is fifteen and a marriage is a thing that happens to somebody in the future.

n8.speaker: torren
n8.text: He'll keep it. He's the sort who keeps things.
n8.direction: Delivered without irony. It should sit very badly for anyone who has read further.

n9.speaker: galbart_glover
n9.text: Aye. That's what worries me and I couldn't tell you why.

n10.speaker: narrator
n10.text: You stand your post for four hours and hear an old man laugh twice, and you learn the terms three days later from a cook, like everybody else.

n11.speaker: narrator
n11.text: The bridge is opened at dawn. It takes the host most of a day to cross it, and Lord Frey watches every single man of them go over, from a window, counting.

scenes.title: The Half That Is Spent
scenes.stage_directions: ACT CLIMAX. CANON: Robb splits his host - Roose Bolton takes the foot south down the kingsroad to meet Tywin at the Green Fork, while Robb takes the horse west to relieve Riverrun. The foot are a feint and everyone in the tent knows it. Torren is assigned to the horse. The scene's job is to make the player understand, plainly and without softening, that the men they have been marching beside for an act are being spent. Composer: the marching ostinato, one last time, and then only hooves.

n1.speaker: robb_stark
n1.text: Lord Bolton takes the foot down the kingsroad. Every man on his feet, every banner, every drum. Make as much noise as twenty thousand men and be seen doing it.

n2.speaker: rickard_karstark
n2.text: Against Tywin Lannister. With foot. Say the rest of it, my lord.

n3.speaker: robb_stark
n3.text: The rest of it is that they will lose, and that while they are losing, six thousand horse will be forty miles west of where Lord Tywin thinks anyone is.

n4.speaker: narrator
n4.text: Nobody argues. That is the part that stays with you. Eleven grown men and a boy of fifteen, and nobody argues, because it is the correct decision and they can all see that it is.

n5.speaker: hune
n5.text: Blackpool's foot go with Lord Bolton. You're a horseman, ser. You go west.

n7.speaker: hune
n7.text: No. You'll go where you're put, and you'll do it without a speech, because a knight who picks his own place in a battle is a knight who's decided the plan is a suggestion. West, ser.

n8.speaker: hune
n8.text: Some of them. The old ones. They've worked it out and they've not said it aloud and they'd thank you not to.

n9.speaker: narrator
n9.text: You say it too quickly and Hune looks at you for a moment before he answers, and you will remember the look longer than the order.

n10.speaker: narrator
n10.text: Serjeant Hune goes west with you. Eighty men of Blackpool go south with Lord Bolton, and you shake perhaps nine of them by the hand before the columns part, and you get the names of six.
n10.direction: The player is given a list of six names on screen. In Act 5, word of the Green Fork arrives and the list is shown again with four crossed off. The four are fixed; the player does not choose.

n11.speaker: robb_stark
n11.text: Ser Torren. Ride near me tomorrow.

n13.speaker: robb_stark
n13.text: Because you carried my brother, and because you're the only man in this camp who doesn't want something from me. Both of those will stop being true. Ride near me while they're still both true.

n14.speaker: narrator
n14.text: The horse rides west at moonrise, six thousand of them, without drums, without banners, without a single torch. It is the most frightening beautiful thing you have ever been part of.
